stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring, $(A,\mathrm d),(B,\mathrm d)$ dg $R$-algebras, and $N$ a dg $(A,B)$-bimodule. The dg Hom functor $M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_B(N,M)$ from $\operatorname{Mod}_{(B,\mathrm d)}$ to $\operatorname{Mod}_{(A,\mathrm d)}$ defines an exact functor
$K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$
of triangulated categories.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule.
conclusions: The dg Hom functor Hom_B(N,-) induces an exact functor of triangulated homotopy categories K(Mod_B) to K(Mod_A).

reason: The dg internal-Hom functor is compatible with shifts and graded-split cone triangles; the cited ABC exactness criterion converts its dg functoriality into an exact functor of homotopy categories.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Here $M$ is any differential graded right $B$-module, viewed as an object of $D(B,\mathrm d)$ as appropriate.

Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be differential graded algebras
over a ring $R$. Let $N$ be a differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule.
Then for every $n \in \mathbf{Z}$ there are isomorphisms
$$
H^n(R\Hom(N, M)) = \Ext^n_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, M)
$$
of $R$-modules functorial in $M$. It is also functorial in $N$
contravariantly under homomorphisms of differential graded $(A,B)$-bimodules (by precomposition on derived Hom).
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule and M a dg right B-module.
conclusions: For every integer n, the cohomology H^n(RHom(N,M)) agrees with Ext^n in D(B) from N to M; this is natural in M and contravariantly in N.

reason: Computes RHom(N,M) as Hom_B(N,I) for a property-(I) replacement M→I. The cited derived-Hom comparison identifies its cohomology with Ext^n_{D(B)}(N,M). Contravariance in N follows by precomposition using the earlier functoriality lemma; the source omits details of the latter.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Property (P) means an exhaustive filtration $0=F_{-1}P\subset F_0P\subset F_1P\subset\cdots$ by dg $A$-submodules with graded-split inclusions and successive quotients isomorphic to direct sums of shifts $A[k]$.

Here $M$ is any differential graded right $B$-module, viewed as an object of $D(B,\mathrm d)$ as appropriate.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential
graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. If
$\Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N') = \Hom_{K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})})}(N, N')$
for all $N' \in K(B, \text{d})$, for example if $N$
has property (P) as a differential graded $B$-module, then
$$
R\Hom(N, M) = \Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(N, M)
$$
functorially in $M$ in $D(B, \text{d})$.
hypotheses:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$ be
differential graded $R$-algebras. Let $N$ be a differential
graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. If
$\Hom_{D(B, \text{d})}(N, N') = \Hom_{K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})})}(N, N')$
for all $N' \in K(B, \text{d})$, for example if $N$
has property (P) as a differential graded $B$-module,
conclusions:
$$
R\Hom(N, M) = \Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(N, M)
$$
functorially in $M$ in $D(B, \text{d})$.

reason: The hypothesis on N makes Hom_B(N,-) preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so the canonical map Hom_B(N,M)→Hom_B(N,I) for an injective replacement is a quasi-isomorphism. Property (P) guarantees that hypothesis via its homotopy-projectivity.
